long_biography.plain_text:
Yaroslavsky entered UkrSibbank as a shareholder in 1995 and later became its president. He helped build the bank into a national institution before transferring control to BNP Paribas and completing his phased exit. The transaction was part of a wider strategy: acquire undervalued businesses, improve them, and sell when their value matured.

In 2007 he formed DCH Investment Management to consolidate and manage his holdings. Its current portfolio crosses iron-ore mining and steelmaking, tractor manufacturing, banking, insurance, property development and hospitality. Specialist executives run the operating companies, while Yaroslavsky remains DCH's owner and president, concentrating on portfolio selection and capital allocation rather than managing every asset day to day.

uncertainties.detail: The Ukrainian form Ярославський is rendered Yaroslavskyi by DCH and Yaroslavsky in the source record; older or Russian-influenced English material uses Alexander Yaroslavsky or Yaroslavskiy. The stored Oleksandr Yaroslavsky is preserved as a legitimate hybrid, while Vladylenovych follows DCH's official English use of the Ukrainian patronymic.

The fortune was built through capital allocation across multiple businesses, with UkrSibbank the landmark documented exit, so Finance & Investments describes creation better than Banking alone. DCH's current holdings span several sectors without a proven dominant one, supporting Diversified as the present industry.

Yaroslavsky founded DCH, but the holding company was created after he had accumulated and sold major assets. It exists to manage his beneficiary portfolio, and specialist executives run the operating businesses. Investor therefore better captures his primary wealth relationship than Founder or Operator.

Official sources establish a move from technical education and academic work into business, but they do not document launch capital, early partners or other material advantages with enough precision to choose the independent or advantaged subtype. Broad Self-made is retained.

Forbes Ukraine has interviewed and ranked Yaroslavsky but no dedicated Forbes person profile was found, so no Forbes social is proposed. DCH directly authenticates one Facebook page. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website cleared the threshold.
